newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Key long bond yields recovered after spiking in the afternoon following the release of worse-than-expected key U.S. payrolls figures which the market had been eagerly awaiting.
The benchmark R150 bond ended the day at 15.36 percent after spiking up to 15.40 percent after the release of the U.S. data and from 15.43 percent overnight.

The U.S. figures, together with the release of the local weekly Treasury bill tender and reserves data were seen providing much needed direction to the market which various dealers described as "trendless".
August U.S. payrolls were up 250,000 against an expected 244,000 and were seen supporting a 25 basis point U.S. rate hike in September.
"Yields briefly spiked up on the figures but recovered on the back of short-covering," a senior trader said, adding that intraday trade had been quiet and volumes on the thin side.
"Even after the release of the U.S. figures the market is not trending and it's difficult to call direction. Now we will be looking out for local reserves figures," he added.
Dealers said a fall in reserves had already been discounted but the market would react if the figure came in significantly out of line with expectations.
Reserves are seen falling to 10.1 billion rand in August from 10.37 billion in July, according to a consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters.

The weekly Treasury bill tender rate, which fell to 15.36 percent from 15.79 percent, was well received by the market. Yields drifted lower to around 15.36 percent immediately after the tender where they lingered ahead of the U.S. data.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 34.05 million rand of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 62.67 million rand of bonds on Thursday. Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 39.17 billion rand on Thursday, a settlement day, from 3.73 billion rand on Wednesday.
On the currency market, early dollar demand saw the rand move above 4.50 on the dollar where it lingered in a tight range for most of the day amid steady two-way trade.
Dealers said the bias was towards further weakness after the 4.47 level held this week.

"A test of 4.5150 is on the cards after 4.47 held very well this week. At this stage 4.51 is looking solid...London banks sold excess dollars back into the market in the afternoon but there is bound to be another test of the softer side eraly next week," one trader at a big bank said.
He added that the day had been characterised by "tight prices" but not much excitement.

At 1419 GMT the rand was at 4.5040/5070 on the dollar from 4.4970/5020 late on Thursday. Against the crosses, it was trading at 7.0376/0499 on sterling from 7.0212/0312 and at 0.3300/3304 marks from 0.3302/3307 marks previously.

On the money market, three-month NCDs inched higher to between 15.90 to 16.10 percent from 15.90 to 16.05 percent, while 90-day BAs were also slightly higher at between 15.35 to 15.50 percent from 15.30 to 15.50 percent.
The Reserve Bank put the money market shortage at 8.949 billion rand on Thursday from 8.532 billion rand on Wednesday.
